audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup repeatedly attributes Volibear's stun to his E ("E hand-of-the-god stun", "E-stun all-in", "E-stun dive"). Volibear has no stun on E.
audit.why: Riot's own kit data gives hardCC to Q only. Thundering Smash (Q): "Volibear gains speed towards enemies, Stunning and damaging the first one he Attacks." Sky Splitter (E): "deals damage and Slows enemies while granting Volibear a Shield if he's inside the blast radius" — slow and self-shield, no CC. A Nasus who saves Wither for a phantom E-stun spends it on the wrong ability and eats the real one.
audit.corrected: The stun is Thundering Smash (Q). Sky Splitter (E) only slows and shields him — and only shields if he is standing inside his own blast.
sources: champ-data/_kits/volibear.json (Riot Data Dragon 16.15.1) — kitFlags.hardCC = ["Q"], E flags = projectile/slow/shield/zone

audit.whatIsWrong: Thundering Smash is called a "Q dash" / "empowered Q dash" in seven separate strings.
audit.why: Q is a movement-speed buff toward enemies whose stun is delivered by a basic attack; it is not a dash. kitFlags.dash lists R only. This is not cosmetic: a dash implies something you sidestep, that crosses terrain, and that grounding stops. A run-down auto-attack stun is none of those — it is unavoidable once he is in attack range, which is exactly why Wither's 700-range point-and-click has to go out during the approach rather than after.
audit.corrected: Thundering Smash is a run-down: he gains speed toward you and his next attack stuns. Stormbringer (R) is his only dash.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet flags zero cooldown-sequencing cues. Nothing anywhere states a real number or a "wait for X before you Y" rule.
audit.why: Thundering Smash is 12/11.5/11/10.5/10 and Wither is 15/14/13/12/11. At the ranks that decide this lane his stun is back up before your answer is — so spending Wither on chip poke leaves a 3s naked window at rank 1. Sky Splitter is a flat 16s at every rank, which is the longest real gap in his kit and the only one that does not shrink as he levels.
audit.corrected: Thundering Smash 12s at rank 1 vs Wither 15s — his stun returns first, so Wither only the committed approach. Sky Splitter is flat 16s at every rank.

audit.whatIsWrong: The late-game text says to respect "his R tower disable and shield".
audit.why: Stormbringer (R) grants bonus Health and disables nearby enemy towers; it does not grant a shield. The shield belongs to Sky Splitter (E). Conflating them makes the reader expect a burst-absorbing layer on the dive that is not there.
audit.corrected: Stormbringer disables your tower and gives him bonus Health. The shield is Sky Splitter's, and only if he lands in his own blast.

audit.whatIsWrong: Grievous Wounds is never mentioned despite Frenzied Maul being the reason he wins extended trades.
audit.why: Frenzied Maul is a flat 5s cooldown and the second cast on a marked target heals him. Over a 10-second duel that is multiple heals against Nasus chip. The late-game text claims Q stacking simply out-paces the heal, which is only reliably true with an anti-heal source.
audit.corrected: Frenzied Maul is 5s flat; his re-bite heal out-paces your chip until you carry a Grievous Wounds source.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer's phase chart and the content layer's chart disagree. Content gives Nasus stages 4-7 (Nasus 4 / Skill 1 / Volibear 2); full gives Volibear stages 1-4, Skill at 6, Nasus only 6-7.
audit.why: Nasus wins this lane 53.23% over 511 games. The content chart matches that shape; the full chart hands Volibear four of seven stages including Levels 4-5, where Wither is already online and the content layer explicitly says the lane has swung. Both charts render, so a reader sees two different answers for the same stage.
audit.corrected: full phases[2].side should be Skill and phases[3].side should be Nasus, matching content win[2] and win[3]. NOT PROPOSED AS AN EDIT — the ±10% length band makes "Volibear" (8) to "Skill"/"Nasus" (5) impossible to submit. Needs applying by hand or a band exemption for enum fields.
sources: champ-data/content/nasus.js win[], champ-data/nasus.full.js phases[].side, packet winRate 53.23 / 511 games

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet suspectNames flags "Spirit Fire's" in mid as a probable wrong ability name (distance 2 from "spirit fire").
audit.why: False positive. Spirit Fire is the correct Riot name for Nasus's E; the edit distance comes from the possessive apostrophe-s. No change needed on that ground.

notes: Two systematic factual errors run through this matchup and are worth checking on every other Nasus-vs-Volibear-shaped entry: (1) the stun attributed to Sky Splitter (E) when it belongs to Thundering Smash (Q), and (2) Thundering Smash described as a dash when Stormbringer (R) is Volibear's only dash. The full-layer phase chart contradicts the content-layer chart at stages 3 and 4 (see audit point 2); I could not submit that fix as an edit because the ±10% length band forbids replacing "Volibear" with "Skill"/"Nasus" in a .side field. Enum-valued paths (.side, .diff, .tone, ratings) probably need a band exemption in the applier, otherwise no chart contradiction anywhere in the dataset is fixable through this pipeline. Packet suspectName "Spirit Fire's" is a false positive.
